Hi Olivia — great questions, thanks for the clarity. Below are three pragmatic options we typically present for accounts at your scale, plus notes on downgrade/upgrade mechanics and where discounts apply. I attached a usage-estimate template to help validate numbers.

Summary (high level)
- Conservative (Team Hosted): start on shared Redwood API (pay-as-you-go), no commit, add Audit Logs + SSO as console add-ons. Works if you want minimal ops and don’t need strict latency SLOs.
- Balanced (Scale Bundle): 12-month annual commit (token commit + reserved concurrency). Includes lower per-token rates, 10% bundled discount, Audit Logs, SSO, and 8 hours/month of priority support. Option to add Dedicated pool at any time with a 30-day lead.
- Aggressive (Enterprise Dedicated): 12–24 month reserved Dedicated capacity, includes private deployment option, SOC2 evidence pack, 20% bundled discount at defined commit levels, custom retention and KMS integration, and 24/7 support.

Downgrade/upgrade notes
- Upgrades: you can move from Team Hosted -> Scale -> Dedicated; we handle model routing and can migrate keys/retention settings with automated runbooks.
- Downgrades: allowed at anniversary with minimal friction but may incur a 30-day transition period for reserved capacity and prorated credits. We do not retroactively remove consumed commit.

Discount mechanics
- Standard annual commit discount: 10% at 12-month commits above $50k ARR equivalent.
- Mid-market (your scale): we can consider up to 15% with a negotiated 12-month commitment and a signed SOW. Anything above 15% requires sales leadership approval (cc’ing Marissa).

Next steps I propose
1) Fill the attached usage_estimate_q1.xlsx and send back (helps us put a firm quote together).
2) I’ll draft three line-item quotes for Procurement with PO language.
3) If you want a trial of Dedicated for 2 weeks, we can scope that as a short-term add-on.

Will loop in Marissa for approval if we need to move past 15% discount. Dev, can you confirm recommended model sizing and any optimizations for the UI latency targets?

Hi team — quick tech notes to help with package selection:

- For sub-200ms median latency at your token sizes, a small Dedicated pool (NVIDIA A10/A100 depending on model) or an optimized hosted path with aggressive batching and prefix caching will be required. Shared hosted can handle initial traffic but expect 200–400ms median.
- Model selection: start with a 7B family quantized to 4-bit for UI use (good latency/cost trade-off). Use a larger 30B for heavy generation backends if you need long-form outputs.
- Cost control levers: prefix caching (saves up to 40% on repeated prompts), continuous batching during non-peak hours, and Redwood Optimize recommendations. Bundling Redwood Optimize as an add-on typically pays for itself within 2–3 months for apps with high repeat patterns.

If you share sample prompt/response sizes in the spreadsheet, I’ll add a recommended instance and estimated token burn per scenario.

—Dev
